verification.scope: Execution and contract checks; business ambiguities require operator answers

notes: The table has 24 rows but only 12 SKUs, because each product appears once for KUL and once for JHB. Group the rows by SKU to produce 12 product records, each with one /prices entry and two /inventory entries (KUL and JHB).
SKU values are zero-padded ('00470001'). Even though the profiler's type sniffing reports int, read them as text: the leading zeros are part of the identifier and must be kept.
Currency MYR and tax rate 5% are copied from explicit source columns, not inferred from KUL/JHB location codes or from retail convention. No FX conversion is applied.
'Tax included' = No with 'Tax rate' = 5% means the /prices amount is VAT-exclusive, so vat_included=false. vat_rate=0.05 is used instead of the schema default 0.07.

No pack size, barcode, category, brand, status, promotion or effective-date columns exist in this export, so those target fields stay unpopulated/defaulted rather than invented. There is also no 'reserved' quantity, so /inventory/*/reserved stays null.
There is no explicit product status column. /status therefore falls back to the contract default 'active' rather than being guessed from the data.

tables.reason: Flat CSV named inventory_export: 24 rows but only 12 distinct SKU values, and each SKU repeats exactly twice, once for Location KUL and once for JHB. The grain is therefore SKU × warehouse stock, with product identity (Product name) and one price list row attached to each stock row. It has to be split into one product per SKU with a /prices entry (standard, net price) and one /inventory entry per location.

columns.name: SKU
columns.reason: Header 'SKU'; values are the item codes 00470001…00470012, each repeated for the two locations. Leading zeros are meaningful text, so they must be kept as a string, never parsed as a number.

columns.name: Product name
columns.reason: Header 'Product name'; one distinct name per SKU ('SIM care 1'…'SIM care 12'). It is the display name and contains no extra detail, so /description stays empty.

columns.name: Currency
columns.reason: Header 'Currency'; the single value MYR is an explicit ISO code in the source, not inferred from the location codes KUL/JHB. It is stated directly in the export.

columns.name: Sales unit
columns.reason: Header 'Sales unit'; the constant value PCS is the base unit of measure and maps directly to the enum_hint value PCS. No pack size is stated anywhere, so /unit/pack_size stays null.

columns.name: Price list
columns.reason: Header 'Price list'; the single value 'standard' matches the contract default and is stated explicitly in the file, so it is copied as-is instead of being assumed.

columns.name: Net price
columns.reason: Header 'Net price'; price-like decimals from 1234.56 to 1356.77, one per row, never empty. It is the per-unit price amount and passes through unchanged. It is not rounded, and no FX conversion is applied even though the currency is MYR.

columns.name: Tax included
columns.reason: Header 'Tax included'; the constant 'No' means the net prices are VAT-exclusive, so vat_included=false (parse_bool). The export states this explicitly, so nothing is inferred from convention.

columns.name: Tax rate
columns.reason: Header 'Tax rate'; the constant '5%' is an explicit source tax rate. parse_number_th with percent_to_fraction gives 0.05, which replaces the contract's 0.07 default because the source states it directly.

columns.name: Location
columns.reason: Header 'Location'; the two values KUL and JHB are the plant/location codes that split the stock, so each becomes a warehouse_code of its own /inventory entry.

columns.name: Available
columns.reason: Header 'Available'; integers from 10 to 41, unique on every row, which matches the SKU × location grain. It is the available stock quantity and is not rounded or altered. There is no reserved/allocated column, so /inventory/*/reserved stays null.

changes_from_draft: Root records deduplicated on /sku (keep first) so the 24 SKU×Location rows collapse to 12 product records, as the grain requires.
/sku now cast to string after trim to guarantee the leading zeros of '00470001' survive; confidence raised to 0.95.
Added the /inventory collection (link on SKU) with warehouse_code = Location (KUL/JHB) and qty = Available; the draft omitted stock entirely although 12 of 24 rows exist only to carry it.
/prices/*/price_list now read from the 'Price list' column (value 'standard' stated in the file) instead of a hard-coded constant.
Added /prices/*/vat_rate = parse_number_th('Tax rate', percent_to_fraction) → 0.05, an explicit source rate replacing the 0.07 schema default.
/prices/*/vat_included now parsed from the 'Tax included' column ('No' → false) instead of a constant.
Added /status = 'active' as the applied contract default; no status column exists in the source, so it is not inferred from data.
Not populated because no source evidence exists: /unit/pack_size, /barcode, /brand, /category, /description, /prices/*/effective_from, /prices/*/effective_to, /inventory/*/reserved, /promotions.
No VAT adjustment applied to amounts: the source states VAT-exclusive prices and the contract only needs the vat_included flag plus the stated rate.
No FX conversion performed; MYR is copied from the explicit Currency column even though the schema default is THB.
